conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-21_strikes/strikes.blend (saved from elements4.blend), scene ST, one station per look (x from 52000, 40 m apart: earth, metal, light, dark, poison). Built by script from the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits plus the new kit vfx_strikes_kit.fbx.
conventions.made: 2026-11-21 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the main body's ground point (y = 0): the body point 3 m out from the player along the line player to body. Pieces with on_player (and ribbons whose centre is player) are relative to the player's ground point. Offsets are world-aligned to the camera (it looks along Unity +z from -z, 55 degrees down).
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body (or in the bowl), p = on the player.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.blade_frame: The charged-blade looks swing a stand-in katana (vfxe3_katana) about the player: it and its sheaths (vfxe3_flameflag_a/b, iceteeth, watersheath, thornvine, stonespine, edgelight, venomcoat) share one frame with the pivot at the hilt end: the blade along local +x (Blender; Unity -x after the axis bake), grip 0 to 0.27 m, guard 0.27 to 0.30 m, blade 0.30 to 1.25 m, the edge facing local +y (Blender), the flat facing up. Their motion.orbit (centre_is player) is the swing: three cuts 0.45 s apart. In Unity, parent the sheath to the real weapon's blade bone with the same frame scaled to the blade length; the orbit keys are the mock-up of the weapon animation, not data to play.
conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (st_stone is lit toon); no stop reaches pure white. The strip maker counts pure-white pixels (all channels 250 or more) in every strip frame (white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.moment: Every look is the infused strike's end effect (L2 + RB): it starts with the cut. t 0 is the blade starting its 170 degree drawing cut (right to left, 0.14 s, blade at 1.05 m, tip 1.55 m out). Pieces are timed to when the blade passes them (stones, clouds) or reaches the enemy (bites, hands, flares), so in Unity start each piece from the swing's own hit times, not a fixed delay, when the weapon is not the katana.
conventions.carrier: Each look keeps the stand-in katana (vfxe3_katana, motion.orbit on the player) only as the mock-up of the swing; it is not part of the look. Nothing in any look is drawn on the blade. The renders also show the cut's path as a thin slate line; it is a reference only and is not in this recipe.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies; 0 is the main body) the piece belongs to: placed about that body and shown on it. Written from the pass's own specs (tools/st_specs.py) by tools/st_assemble_recipe.py. Pieces on the player carry on_player instead.
conventions.per_struck_enemy: motion.per_struck_enemy = true marks a piece that exists once for each enemy the cut actually hits, about that enemy (its motion.body is the stand-in it was drawn on). Spawn one set per struck enemy and none on a miss. Bodies 0 to 2 are the struck stand-ins (struck_bodies), body 3 is outside the cut (missed_bodies) and has nothing drawn on it in any look. Dark is built only of such pieces.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment (infused), owner (the comment and the fix it answers, quoted), answer (how the look answers them), look (in words), revision_of (what it replaces in game), struck_bodies, missed_bodies and per_struck_enemy_pieces.
conventions.revisions: 2026-11-21. Round 3: Earth and Metal approved; Light, Dark and Poison redone. Round 4: Light approved; Dark and Poison redone. Round 5: Dark approved after one fix (organic merged hands, outline on the outer silhouette only, done here); Poison redone as a flat vein web on the skin and dull dark drops and round pools with no highlight dot. Earth, Metal and Light entries are unchanged since their approval. Earlier versions: v1/, v2/, v3/.
conventions.dark_hands_outline: Dark's hands (vfxst_hand_big_open, vfxst_hand_big_grip: one rounded organic mesh each; material st_hand_small, near-black with a violet rim) were rendered with a violet outline on their outer silhouette (Freestyle line set InkHands, colour 0.42, 0.18, 0.7 linear, thickness 1.5). Each hand is one merged mesh, so the outline never traces joins between parts. In Unity give them an outline pass in that colour on the silhouette only.
conventions.poison_veins: Poison's bruise, wound, vein web and sheen are ribbons whose points were snapped onto the stand-in body's surface and sunk into it so they lie flat on the skin (the bruise shows as a flat patch about 1.5 cm proud, the fine vessels as painted lines) and ride its motion (follow_body). In Unity build them as a decal or a vein and bruise mask in the enemy's shader that spreads from the wound with the same timing; nothing should stand out of the body.

owner: 2026-11-21, Earth (Massive Sword, infused strike): "Good but not sure if this coincides too much with the elemental spells and whatnot. Does it make sense for the heavy to have the element cast?"

The owner's answer (2026-11-21): keep an element effect, but it must grow out of the blade's cut (along the slash line and where it hits), so it reads as a sword move and never like a spell being cast. Earth: the stones rise along the arc of the cut, not as a separate Broken Ground line ahead.
looks.answer: No line running ahead: seven chunky faceted stones (0.66 to 0.76 m across, 0.8 to 1.2 m tall, cel-shaded and inked) heave up out of the floor along the arc the blade just swept, one after another right behind it, so the cut itself throws them up. The three it reached are thrown up off the stones; the stones hold 0.6 s, shudder and settle back down with a last puff of dust, and nothing is left on the floor.
looks.look: The cut tears the ground along its own arc: chunky stones heave up one after another right behind the blade, leaning out, throwing the enemies it reached up off their feet. Chips fly and dust bursts round them; they hold, shudder, and settle back into the floor.

owner: 2026-11-21, Metal (Massive Sword, infused strike): "The final effect on the heavy charge needs to be fully reworked but the swings are good"

The fix (2026-11-21): scrap the disc and its dashed rings. The cut leaves a bright steel glint along its edge, and a spray of small steel shards rings off whatever it hits. The owner's Metal rule: only a glint or a small forged blade.
looks.answer: No disc, no rings, nothing on the floor but falling shards. One bright steel glint (pale steel blue, never white) runs along the cut's edge as a short streak right behind the blade and flares once at its end. Where the edge bites an enemy, a hard glint flashes and nine small forged steel shards and five steel sparks ring off it along the direction of the cut, spin, fall and lie a moment before they go.
looks.look: The edge bites with a hard steel glint and a spray of small steel shards rings off each enemy it hits, spinning and clattering to the floor. A bright steel glint runs the length of the cut right behind the blade and flares once at the end. The shards lie a moment and are gone.

owner: 2026-11-21, Light (Massive Sword, infused strike): "good, but on the final swing, the half circle that spawns is terrible needs a full scrap and then rework"

The owner on the v1 strip (2026-11-21): "from the cut": no sky beam at all. The cut itself leaves a line of warm glare along the slash path. It flares on each struck enemy and breaks into drifting motes. Warm gold and amber, never white, and no floor shapes.
looks.answer: No beam and nothing from the sky: the cut itself leaves a line of warm gold glare along its own path at blade height (an amber line riding just outside it), drawn with the blade, glints flashing on it as the blade passes. Where the cut meets an enemy it flares in a burst of warm rays that breaks into motes drifting up off it. A moment after the cut the glare line breaks up from its tail into gold and amber motes that drift up and out and go out. Nothing touches the floor, and no colour is white.
looks.look: The cut leaves a line of warm gold glare along its path, glints flashing on it. Each enemy it meets flares in a burst of warm rays. Then the glare breaks up from its tail into gold and amber motes that drift up and fade.

owner: 2026-11-21, Dark (Massive Sword, infused strike): "Good but the charged effect after the swing needs to be scrapped and reworked"

The owner on the v1 strip (2026-11-21): many small, clearly hand-shaped hands clutch at each struck enemy's legs from its shadow and tug downward together. Don't actually move the enemy into the floor; it stays on the floor and only strains or stumbles in place.

The owner on the v2 strip (2026-11-21): "fewer, bigger hands": 2 or 3 big, clearly human hands per struck enemy (open palm, five distinct fingers, a thumb), black with a thin violet rim; they grip the shins and tug down; the enemy stays on the floor and only strains. At the game camera they must read as hands, not spider legs: fewer and larger shapes, fingers thick enough to see at 12 m, and the palm visible.

The owner on the v3 strip (2026-11-21): approved after one fix: smooth the big hands into rounded, organic hands (soft knuckles, tapered fingers, a curved palm, no boxy blocks), and the violet rim traces only the outer silhouette, never the joins between parts.
looks.answer: Three big shadow hands per struck enemy (new stk_hand_big: one rounded, organic mesh per hand, with a cupped palm 0.45 m wide at the size used, soft knuckles, four tapered fingers and a thumb, about 1.05 m long; black with a thin violet rim, and a violet outline on its outer silhouette only), spaced apart on the side the camera sees so they never overlap. They come up out of seeps of its shadow low, reaching in to its shins at about 35 degrees so the broad flat of each hand and all five digits face the game camera; open palms first, then they grip the shins with the fingers half closed (still apart) and tug down together three times. The enemy stays on the floor: it squashes a little and lurches with each tug while the hands dip. Then they let go and sink back, and the shadow closes. Nothing is drawn on a miss; every piece is per struck enemy.
looks.look: The moment the cut lands, the struck enemy's shadow pools dark and three big black hands, rimmed in violet, reach up out of it, palms open. They grip its shins and tug it down, again and again; it strains but stays on its feet. Then they let go and sink back into the shadow. A miss draws nothing.

strip: the cut lands; round drops of venom spatter off each enemy it struck
they splash on the floor; the skin bruises round the wound
a dark web of veins spreads flat over the skin; the drops pool and bubble
a faint sickly sheen slides along the veins
veins, bruise and dark pools
they fade and the pools soak in; the one outside untouched
owner: 2026-11-21, Poison (Massive Sword, infused strike): "Good but the charged effect after the swing is old poison visuals and needs to be completely reworked"

The owner on the v1 strip (2026-11-21): no clouds off the swing. Where the cut lands, dark green veins spread across the struck enemy's body from the wound, on the body surface, pulsing. On impact, dark green venom spatters off the enemy onto the floor. Per struck enemy only.

The owner on the v2 strip (2026-11-21): "darker, liquid drops": round, wet, near-black-green drops that splash and pool, not pointed leaf shapes. Veins: dark bulging lines that bruise the skin around the wound, with a faint sickly sheen. Nothing plant-like: no sprouts or leaf silhouettes; it must not be mistaken for Life. Deep greens only.

The owner on the v3 strip (2026-11-21): "the veins on the person looks almost like green roots growing out of them ... and the drops that pool have a small light green dot in them making it look like sprouts almost". The veins must lie flat on the skin as a dark discoloured web spreading from the wound (short, fine, flat lines, nothing standing out, no thick branching tubes); no light highlight in the drops or pools; nothing may read as roots, sprouts or plants.
looks.answer: Liquid and dark, nothing plant-like. Where the cut lands on each struck enemy a near-black wound opens and the skin bruises dark round it, flat on the skin. From it a web of short, fine, flat lines (poisoned blood vessels, three generations each finer than the last, half sunk into the skin so nothing stands out) spreads over the body in dark green-black, and a faint, dull, sickly green sheen slides along the main ones twice. On impact eight round near-black-green drops (new stk_drop: a dull dark sheen at the edge, no bright spot) spatter off along the cut and away from you, splash on the floor with round droplets and spread into round dark pools that bubble and pop, then soak in a little. No highlight dots, no sprouts, no wisps, no lobed or pointed shapes; every colour is a deep or near-black green.
looks.look: Where the cut lands, the skin bruises dark round the wound and a fine dark web of poisoned veins spreads flat across the enemy's body, a faint sickly sheen sliding along it. Round drops of near-black venom spatter off onto the floor, splash, and spread into round dark pools that bubble.
looks.revision_of: poison infused strike (the elements 2 look, StrikeArt.cs:153-164); replaces the 2026-11-21 v1 clouds and v2 green spatter
